items.title: Railways to separate Mangaluru region from Palakkad: Kerala upset, K’taka BJP hails move
items.summary: Follow TNM's WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. The Railway Board has decided to merge the Mangaluru railway region with the South Western Railway’s Mysuru division with effect from October 1. The move is expected to significantly undermine the operational and financial importance of the Palakkad division. The Railway Board’s decision has sparked opposition in Kerala, with many political leaders, including Chief Minister VD Satheesan, openly criticising the move. The move would cause revenue and operational losses to the Palakkad division, they said. Meanwhile, the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) in Karnataka is celebrating the Railway Board decision. The Palakkad railway division is headquartered in Olavakkode, Palakkad, and forms one of the six administrative divisions under the Southern Railway zone. Established in 1956, it is one of India's oldest railway divisions, managing transit networks across Kerala, Tamil Nadu, and Karnataka. Formed as the Olavakkode division by dissolving the Podanur division in 1979, it spanned nearly 1,248 route km.
